To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Finnish organic food system should be developed to meet consumer values and the goals set by government.
the organic food chain in Finland has not reached its goals because the stakeholders have not taken into consideration the consumer values in their decision-making and planning.
the Finnish organic food system has not developed sufficiently due to the lack of co-operation between the actors, which has resulted in poor food quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Finnish organic food system, and the results can be applied to the conventional food system, too.
how to make food production and the food system more sustainable.
how the Finnish organic food supply chain could be improved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the food industry needs to be reformed to meet the needs of the consumers, and the organic food chain needs to be restructured in order to achieve the goals set by stakeholders.

by using the principles of the Economy of Common Goods Theory in the Finnish organic food production, the organic food chain will develop more efficiently and the production and consumption goals set for it will be achieved.

by using the Economy of the Common Good Theory and Activity Theory Model as a tool, the Finnish organic food industry can be developed in a way that will benefit consumers and the food chain stakeholders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Economy of Common good theory and Yrjö’s Activity Theory model could be used to develop the organic food chain in Finland.
the Finnish organic food production and food chain could be developed to meet consumer values and needs and thus increase the volume of production, consumption, and sales.
the organic food chain needs to be restructured to meet the goals of all its stakeholders, including the consumers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the organic food chain should be evaluated based on qualitative factors and that the consumer should be a part of the food chain.
the food chain should be evaluated from a consumer point of view.
the food chain should not be viewed only as a chain of production and distribution, but also as a process of creating food and a community of people who create it.
